quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your entire face, not just your eyes.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes. Goggles only protect your eyes, not the rest of your face. A windshield is not a good substitute for either.

questions.question: Can common drugs like cold tablets affect your ability to ride safely?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your ability to safely operate a motorcycle.
Usually they will not affect your ability to safely operate a motorcycle.
No, they pose no risk to your operating ability.
No, they are always safe to take before riding because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your ability to safely operate a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Before taking any drug, learn about its side effects and how it may impact your riding.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Make sudden moves.
Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden movements, stay away from the road edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees that the driver will yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee that the driver will yield to you.
It means the driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee that the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that eye contact with another driver means they will yield to you or give you the right-of-way. Do not count on it for your safety.

questions.question: How should the front brake be used?

options.text: It is too dangerous for inexperienced riders to use.
It is best to use it alone.
It should occasionally assist the rear brake.
It should be used together with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly on a motorcycle?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the same side as your intended turn. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction once you are clear of the hazard.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar during motorcycle acceleration?

options.text: It feels like it is lagging behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
It vibrates uncontrollably.
It makes acceleration seem faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is lagging behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. Due to its inertia, it feels like it lags behind when you accelerate.

questions.question: What should you do with the handgrip when turning a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it can be dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: When riding faster than walking speed, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Pressing the grip in the direction you want to turn causes the proper lean.

questions.question: What can help reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only about five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others by using your signals and brake light. Keep a safe distance around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides of your vehicle. Always be prepared to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, what should you do?

options.text: Brake using the tire that is not flat.
Brake using the tire that is flat.
Brake using both tires.
Do not use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake using the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat and you must brake, slowly apply the brake to the tire that is not flat (if you are sure which one it is).

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what is correct?

options.text: You must finish passing without going over the speed limit.
You can finish passing in a no-passing zone if you started before the zone.
You can go over the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must finish passing without going over the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done at or below the speed limit and only where passing is allowed.

questions.question: Is braking in a turn easier or harder than braking on a straight road?

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe only if you use the front brake only.
Safe only if you use the rear brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes while turning, but you need proper technique and must be very careful.

questions.question: Before you carry a passenger in traffic for the first time, what should you do?

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice riding on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others see you.
Practice riding on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice riding on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before carrying a passenger or heavy load in traffic for the first time, practice on a quiet road. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: When should you keep more space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: When roads are slippery.
When it is sunny outside.
When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.correctAnswerText: When roads are slippery.
questions.explanation: Keep a two-second gap between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Keep a larger gap when conditions make it harder to stop, such as on wet or icy roads.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest and you operate it with your left foot. Lift the lever to shift to a higher gear. Press it down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: When riding at night, how fast should you travel?

options.text: Slower than you would during the day under similar conditions.
The same speed as you would during the day under similar conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under similar conditions.
On the road shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night than you would during the day under the same weather and traffic conditions. It is harder to see hazards in the dark, so going slower helps you avoid them.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where in the lane should you position yourself?

options.text: Always avoid the left portion of the lane.
Always avoid the right portion of the lane.
Always avoid the center portion of the lane.
Use the safest position for the road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the safest position for the road conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on the road conditions around you.

questions.question: Where should you get the main information about your motorcycle?

options.text: From the motorcycle's former owner.
From the owner's manual.
From a library book about motorcycles.
From a motorcycle enthusiast.

questions.correctAnswerText: From the owner's manual.
questions.explanation: The owner's manual is your best source of information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before operating your motorcycle for the first time.

questions.question: At what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person considered legally intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: A person age 21 or older with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to operate a vehicle while intoxicated.

questions.question: A motorcycle horn can:

options.text: Does not work.
Cannot be heard by other people.
Alert someone quickly.
Should never be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alert someone quickly.
questions.explanation: A horn can help you get someone's attention fast. However, a motorcycle horn is quieter than a car horn. Other drivers may not hear it. Do not depend only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull over and stop until the rain ends.
Ride where car tires have left tracks.
Go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride where car tires have left tracks.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of a wet lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left track often works best, but it depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: When you carry a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean when you lean.
Hold the motorcycle seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: A passenger should lean with you during turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking your control. They should hold onto passenger handles or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Keep riding—it will stop on its own.
Brake hard quickly.
Release the throttle to slow down.
Go faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the throttle to slow down.
questions.explanation: Speeding up will make the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars tight and slowly release the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Then find and fix the problem causing the wobble.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means:

options.text: The operator plans to turn left.
The operator is about to stop.
The operator plans to turn right.
The operator is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The operator plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Instead of turn signals, operators can use hand signals. If an operator's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means they plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.
